text: The board suspended the $750m buyback program and committed all excess cashh to balance-sheet reinforcement while maintaining an 8.320¢ dividend. Q4 profit was $1.54bn; full-year profit $7.49bn. Net debt fell to $22.18bn, operating cash flow was $7.6bn, and 2026 capex was set at $13-13.5bn as shares dropped ~4%.

meta.note: Commodity-price pressure sits at the boundary of Corporate vs. Macro-Economy.

text: Revenue missed expectations ($11.82B vs $12.03B), yet organic revenue rose 5% and unit case volume rose 1% for a second straight quarter. Management guided to 4-5% organic revenue growth and 7-8% comparable EPS growth for 2026. Volume improved in North America (+1%) and Latin America (+2%), while sparkling drinks were flat and water/sports/coffee/tea grew 3%. Net income was $2.27B; EPS $0.58 adjusted.

meta.note: Demand improvement and weakness coexist across product segments.

text: December retail sales were flat month-to-month (0.0%) after +0.6% in November; ex-autos were also flat. Annual growth slowed to 2.4% (3.3% ex-autos), and the GDP "control group" fell 0.1%. Multiple categories declined (furniture -0.9%, apparel -0.7%, electronics -0.4%), while online rose only 0.1% and building materials +1.2%. CPI ran at 2.7% for the month.

meta.note: Retail softness coexistd with strong Q4 GDP signals, creating classification tension.

text: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick acknowledged under oath that he and his family had lunch on Jeffrey Epstein's private island in 2012, contradicting prior claims that contact ended in 2005. Newly released DOJ files show communications continuing through at least 2012-2014. Senators pressed him to provide his records to Congress while he denied any wrongdoing and described only seeing household staff on the island.

meta.note: Boundary between personal conduct and official credibility was structurally ambiguous.

text: Q4 adjusted EPS came in at $0.13 versus $0.19 expected, cutting EBIT from a previously signaled $7.7B to $6.8B after ~$900M in tariff costs and supply disruptions from the Novelis aluminum fire. For 2026, Ford set higher targets (EBIT $8-10B; FCF $5-6B; capex $9.5-10.5B) while projecting roughly flat net tariff exposure (~$2B). 2025 revenue reached a record $187.3B, but the year ended with an $8.2B net loss after $15.5B in special charges tied to an EV pullback.

meta.note: Accounting "special items" separate headline loss from core operations.
